content:
Yuki Sato: hey all — want to sync on kernel autoselect heuristics before I bake them into ADR-019 + PR. Specifically: FP8 vs INT8 vs baseline, and what guardrails we need to keep rollout safe.

Hiro Tanaka: +1. we should be explicit about (a) which ops we’re swapping (attn vs matmul) and (b) what signals we use at runtime (gpu arch, head_dim, hidden size, seq regime).

Noah Patel: also need a clear failure mode: if anything is ambiguous or unsupported, we fall back to baseline. don’t “try and pray” in prod.

Grace Kim: what we have from the microbench side so far (very rough):
- H100: FP8 attention is best for decode-heavy + mid/long seq, but can regress TTFT in short prompts (launch overhead dominates)
- A100: INT8 matmul gains are consistent on MLP for common shapes, but attention FP8 is spottier / more shape constraints
- L4: INT8 matmul helps a lot, but we have to be conservative with alignment + saturation edge cases

Rina Kobayashi: from harness runs: the biggest “oops” cases are weird head_dim / GQA variants and long-context prefill (cache pressure). if dispatch doesn’t gate those, we get noisy p95.

Claire Dubois: can we define the heuristics in terms of measurable regimes?
1) GPU capability set (H100/Hopper vs A100/Ampere vs L4/Ada)
2) Shape constraints (head_dim ∈ {64, 128}, hidden_size multiple-of-128, etc.)
3) Workload regime (prefill-dominant vs decode-dominant; short vs long context)
4) Risk controls (eval signoff required? canary only?)
I want this to be defensible in the benchmark methodology doc.

Yuki Sato: yep. proposal v0:
- default baseline everywhere
- allow FP8 attention only on H100 initially, gated by: head_dim in {64,128} AND seq_len_decode >= 128 OR (prefill_tokens >= 512 AND batch >= 4)
- allow INT8 matmul on H100 + A100 + L4 for MLP GEMMs when: K and N aligned (multiple-of-64), and activation quant path is “verified” for model family
- anything else falls back

Sofia Ivanova: question: why the seq_len_decode >= 128 cut? end-to-end we saw FP8 attention win on TPOT for smaller decode too, but TTFT got worse because scheduler mixed prefill/decode and paid extra launch overhead.

Omar El-Sayed: +1. the scheduler interleaving matters. if the queue is prefill-heavy, FP8 attn might not realize wins and could hurt TTFT. we need to factor in “mix” not just raw seq_len.

Marcus Reed: we now have prefill/decode split metrics in the branch (per-request + aggregated). we could use a runtime “mode” signal: if prefill_fraction > X in last N seconds for the route, prefer baseline for attn.

Noah Patel: i’m nervous about using dynamic feedback for *dispatch* (flappy). could use it only as a rollout gate / canary signal, not in-line selection.

Hiro Tanaka: agree. keep dispatch purely static (gpu + shape + requested config). use canary to decide whether to expand eligibility.

Rafael Mendes: from SRE side: static rules + flags are much easier to reason about. if a canary spikes TTFT we want deterministic rollback.

Yuki Sato: ok. so dispatch heuristics = static. we’ll incorporate workload regime by using request-visible numbers only (prompt len, max_new_tokens, batch) not feedback.

Grace Kim: re: “short prompts TTFT regression” — it’s not only prompt len. it’s also concurrency. low QPS makes overhead more visible. but agree we shouldn’t build a control system in dispatch.

Claire Dubois: then we should document that we’re optimizing for production traffic distribution and protecting tail latency with gating + rollback, rather than attempting perfect per-request optimality.

Rina Kobayashi: edge cases we MUST gate:
- head_dim=96 (some models)
- odd KV cache layouts (we already hit alignment issues once)
- very long context (>= 16k) prefill — we saw occasional OOM-ish behavior when temp buffers expand

Hiro Tanaka: + mention: some kernels require specific CUDA/driver combos. if runner pins versions but prod fleet differs by region, we need a guard: only enable if driver >= X and cuda runtime >= Y (or container image tag matches).

Keiko Yamamoto: fleet note: eu-west H100 pool is on the newer driver, us-east has a mixed batch right now. if we don’t gate by image/driver we’ll get region-specific weirdness.

Yuki Sato: good call. we can gate via “runtime build + cuda minor” since we control the container. i’ll avoid raw driver checks if possible.

Marcus Reed: what about model-family gating? ex: MoE variants vs dense, GQA vs MHA. we should not assume “hidden size multiple-of-128” is enough.

Grace Kim: we can do:
- FP8 attention eligible only for model_arch in {llama-like dense attention} initially
- INT8 matmul eligible for {llama-like, mistral-like} (whatever our top hosted set is) and explicitly exclude MoE

Noah Patel: +1. keep allowlist tight. “top 6 hosted models” first. then expand when we have data.

Rafael Mendes: rollout plan suggestion:
1) flags default OFF
2) enable in perf canary only (one region, small %)
3) add auto-rollback on TTFT p95 + error rate + correctness counters
4) expand region-by-region

Sofia Ivanova: can we at least allow INT8 matmul on A100 by default for the known-safe shapes? seems low risk and we already have fallback.

Claire Dubois: quality risk is the question. INT8 can be fine but we need Applied ML signoff criteria. if it’s “no default until eval signoff”, we should reflect that.

Yuki Sato: my understanding: INT8 default enablement requires eval signoff per model family; but we can still ship the kernel + dispatch behind a server flag.

Hiro Tanaka: exactly. ship capability; decide default policy later.

Rina Kobayashi: implementation detail: dispatch should log/emit a single dimension tag like kernel_mode={baseline,fp8,int8} and kernel_variant id. otherwise debugging canary diffs is a pain.

Marcus Reed: already in flight for metrics tagging. once that lands, perf canary can slice on model/gpu/mode.

Grace Kim: can we add a hard “kill switch” per model + per region? (not just global) so we can hotfix-disable one bad shape without rolling back everything.

Rafael Mendes: yes please. we’ve been burned by global toggles. per model/region cohort is the right granularity.

Noah Patel: heuristics summary i’d be comfortable with:
- Baseline default
- FP8 attention: H100 only, allowlisted models only, head_dim in {64,128}, exclude long-context initially (e.g., prompt_tokens > 8k => baseline), require runtime build >= 1.22.0
- INT8 matmul: allowlisted models, strict alignment constraints, exclude MoE, exclude known-bad shapes, fallback on any guard failure
- everything behind flags with per-model/region overrides

Claire Dubois: add: definition of “known-bad shapes” has to live somewhere (config/registry) + we should cite it in ADR as “guardrail list maintained by kernel team”. otherwise it becomes tribal knowledge.

Yuki Sato: 👍. I’ll encode allowlist + exclusions in kernel registry metadata (so it’s reviewable), and ADR points to the registry keys.

Hiro Tanaka: action items?

Yuki Sato: actions:
- Yuki: update ADR-019 draft with above + explicit guardrails + rollout steps
- Hiro/Grace: confirm initial allowlist models + shape constraints from microbench results
- Rina: ensure harness covers head_dim=96 + long-context cases so we prove fallback works
- Rafael: sanity check canary rollback triggers (TTFT p95, TPOT p95, error rate) and required tagging

Rafael Mendes: sounds good. please include comms snippet for #eng-sre when we flip canary.

Sofia Ivanova: last note: scheduler knobs can mask kernel wins. when we report results, we should separate “kernel-only” vs “end-to-end w/ tuned scheduling”.

Claire Dubois: +1, and footnote it. otherwise we’ll get pinged on “why don’t my numbers match”.

Yuki Sato: ack. I’ll keep ADR scoped to dispatch + guardrails, and link to scheduler notes separately.

Hiro Tanaka: :thumbsup: ship it (carefully).
